findings.description: The bucket has no ACL specified (defaulting to potential public exposure per the comment noting it is public) and lacks any public access block configuration, exposing customer data to unauthenticated internet access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket, including a customer master file, are stored unencrypted.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of sensitive customer data cannot be recovered, and combined with force_destroy, data loss risk is amplified.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in unencrypted public bucket
findings.description: A customer master spreadsheet (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted.
Versioning is not enabled for the financials bucket, risking irreversible data loss or tampering, especially combined with force_destroy = true.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so operational data is stored unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving data science datasets unencrypted at rest.
